decision_checklist.summary: Keep skb_shared_info refcount splits and header-write eligibility explicitly in C.
decision_checklist.rationale: The split dataref model and header-clone rules decide whether headers may be mutated at all, so they are core ownership logic rather than a safe Phase 14 wrapper target.

decision_checklist.summary: Keep destructor callbacks and final release ordering explicitly in C.
decision_checklist.rationale: Teardown crosses destructor callbacks, destructor_arg payloads, frag lists, and final consume or free paths, which is exactly the kind of lifetime ownership Phase 14 should record and leave in C.

decision_checklist.summary: Track partial-GSO metadata rewrites and the final sock-owned tail transfer before segmented output ownership leaves the bridge study boundary.
decision_checklist.rationale: skb_segment() promotes NETIF_F_GSO_PARTIAL into SKB_GSO_PARTIAL, clears SKB_GSO_DODGY, rewrites each segment's gso_size, gso_segs, gso_type, and SKB_GSO_CB(iter)->data_offset, then transfers sock-owned backpressure state by swapping the tail skb truesize, destructor, and sk with head_skb when head_skb->destructor == sock_wfree, so Zigux should keep both the partial-seg metadata path and the tail-owner transfer in C while only naming the handoff.

decision_checklist.summary: Track the checksum-to-data-offset crossover that seeds each output skb before later tail publication.
decision_checklist.rationale: skb_segment() carries checksum state forward by seeding SKB_GSO_CB(nskb)->csum and SKB_GSO_CB(nskb)->csum_start, rewrites SKB_GSO_CB(iter)->data_offset as the remaining bytes shrink, and only later publishes the tail chain through segs->prev with remcsum_offload in play, so Zigux should keep this checksum-to-publication crossover in C while only recording the boundary.

decision_checklist.summary: Record the exported tail-list publication contract before segmented output leaves skb_segment() for xmit-list consumers.
decision_checklist.rationale: skb_segment() only publishes the accumulated list tail after wiring segs->prev and finalizing the last segment's gso_size or gso_segs clamp, then hands that exported list to validate_xmit_skb_list() under the existing qdisc and xmit ownership model, so Zigux should keep tail publication and downstream consumer coordination in C while only recording the contract.

gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 14 build gate now needs one more bounded module so the skbuff study lane becomes reviewable without widening into a fake port.
The existing make target keeps the skbuff bridge lane runnable with the same bounded discipline as the other Phase 14 studies.

The first honest skbuff foothold is a boundary map around __alloc_skb(), napi_alloc_skb(), skb_clone(), pskb_expand_head(), __skb_checksum_complete(), skb_segment(), and consume_skb(), with explicit stay-in-C decisions where shared-data ownership and teardown are still too coupled to refcounts and destructors.

The bridge and manifest now carry the exact four roadmap boundary-study area ids, so later runs can prove roadmap alignment from structured packet-local data instead of inferring intent from array order or broad survey wording.
A dedicated Phase 14 test gate is the smallest truthful way to lock the new boundary map to its manifest and keep later runs from drifting into fake implementation claims.
The slice note records the exact boundary-map posture so the lane does not overstate symbol cataloging as skbuff ownership.
The survey note compares the 7,476-line skbuff anchor, its 5,467-line public header, and a nearby datagram user against the new bridge so future runs stay honest about what still belongs in C.

The skbuff bridge now needs one explicit packet-local checklist that turns the existing stay-in-C decisions around dataref ownership, consume_skb() teardown, and the qdisc-facing skb_segment() publication checkpoints into machine-checkable evidence instead of leaving those decisions implied across code and prose.

The bridge now carries a small lifetime audit outline plus a concurrency-sensitive checkpoint catalog around dataref splits, pskb_expand_head() clone-or-reallocate handoff, destructor_arg and frag-list teardown, checksum-complete state caching, and the tail-publication checkpoints inside skb_segment(), so Zigux can satisfy the roadmap's concurrency-audit requirement without claiming live allocator, refcount, checksum, qdisc, or destructor control.

The bridge now separates checksum-complete state around __skb_checksum_complete() and skb_checksum_complete_unset() so the lane can name skb->csum, skb->ip_summed, skb->csum_valid, and skb->csum_complete_sw without claiming live checksum-state ownership.

The bridge now makes segmentation handoff explicit around skb_segment(), skb_orphan_frags(), skb_zerocopy_clone(), SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG propagation, CHECKSUM_NONE fallback, and SKB_GSO_CB(nskb) checksum metadata so the lane records how frag ownership and checksum state move without weakening the current stay-in-C posture.

The bridge now records the smaller skb_segment() partial-seg metadata rewrite and tail-owner transfer around SKB_GSO_PARTIAL, SKB_GSO_DODGY, SKB_GSO_CB(iter)->data_offset, and sock_wfree so the lane names the remaining backpressure handoff without widening into live packet lifetime control.

The bridge now records the checksum-to-data-offset crossover inside skb_segment(), limited to SKB_GSO_CB(nskb)->csum, SKB_GSO_CB(nskb)->csum_start, SKB_GSO_CB(iter)->data_offset, and remcsum_offload so the lane can name the remaining checksum-to-data-offset coupling without widening into live packet lifetime control.

The bridge now records the exported tail-publication contract inside skb_segment(), limited to segs->prev, the last-segment gso_size or gso_segs clamp, tail->next publication, and validate_xmit_skb_list() so the lane names the remaining qdisc-facing consumer handoff without widening into live packet lifetime control.

Live skbuff allocation, dataref transitions, checksum-state caching, destructor-driven teardown, frag-list ownership, segmentation metadata updates, and GSO tail-owner transfer remain blocked until Phase 14 has much stronger stay-in-C evidence and still keeps those mechanisms in the existing C implementation.
